newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea signs investment accord with Russia.
newsitem.headline: North Korea signs investment accord with Russia.

text.p: North Korea said on Monday it had signed an agreement with Russia on the promotion and mutual protection of investment.

"An agreement on encouragement and mutual protection of investment between the governments of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea and Russia was signed on Nov 28," the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said in a report monitored in Tokyo.
The pact was signed in Moscow by the Korean ambassador to Russia, Son Song-phil, and Russia's Economy Minister Yevgeni Yasin, KCNA said. The report gave no more details on the agreement.

The accord follows a report last month by Russia's Itar-Tass news agency that Russia and North Korea would begin discussions on a new bilateral treaty to strengthen ties frayed since the collapse of the Soviet Union.

Tass quoted Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Grigory Karasin as saying the accord would be "an important step towards the further development of equal, mutually beneficial cooperation between both countries".
Karasin added that Russia had a strong interest in promoting stability on its Far Eastern borders, Tass reported.
"The most important thing is not to allow an escalation of tension in the region and to renew the inter-Korean peace process," Tass quoted him as saying.

Tass also reported that Karasin cast doubt on the usefulness of a U.S. proposal for talks involving North and South Korea, China and the United States. He suggested that a wider forum, including Russia, Japan and the United Nations, should be convened.
